scope: On-device measurements only. Source analysis is assigned to Claude. No new functional display patch, build, flash, reboot, display write or power transition during the passive capture.

physical_observation.before_previous_replay: User reported totally black after fresh recovery boot.
physical_observation.after_replay_and_during_passive_baseline: User confirmed Black screen without pressing buttons.

driver_vs_manual.method: Kprobe at msm:dsi_host_transfer records message type, flags, tx length and first two payload bytes; return probe records transfer result. DPU kickoff events are recorded in the same trace.
driver_vs_manual.observation: No DPU kickoff occurred between step 2 and step 3 in this replay. The timer delay did not ensure a new frame started between the two steps.
limits: Both sequences were executed in the same already-failed state. This is not a matched successful-vs-failed comparison.
Host-entry values and nonnegative transfer returns do not prove that the panel accepted or latched a setting.
Only the first two bytes of the 34-byte gamma packet were captured. The ten normal-setting packets are each two bytes and were captured completely.
A replay after boot is not a cold-boot initialization trace.
The kickoff-only trace does not prove absence of a completion from an earlier in-flight frame.

passive_baseline.observation: Nine DPU kickoffs each had a transmit-done callback on both pingpong blocks and a CRTC frame-done event, while the user still saw black. No enabled timeout or underrun event was recorded. The trace reports 57 entries written and 57 retained.
limits: These callbacks show the SoC display pipeline completing work; they do not prove valid panel scanout or visible emission.
The aggregate MDSS interrupt delta is not proof of a particular TE frequency or source.
A 20-second capture cannot exclude intermittent failures outside its window.
There was no forced refresh or pixel-content change; recovery continued its own normal UI activity.

conclusions: The latest physical display failure remains unresolved. Neither lower power draw nor successful host writes proves it is fixed.

The ten normal-setting packets no longer differ between driver and manual HS paths in package 25. The earlier package-23 hard-coded LP bug was real, but is insufficient to explain the current failure.
The black screen can coexist with completed frame work on both pingpong blocks. It is not explained by absence of all framebuffer updates during this measurement.
A real frame-event ordering hypothesis is worth comparing to stock, but the measured gap alone is not a proven root cause.
pending_source_questions: Which actual frame event(s) must precede display-on, compression or brightness latching, and which events must follow them?
Which complete brightness batch, command grouping and master/slave delivery semantics does stock require, beyond the ten ACL/ELVSS packets?
Which state must survive or be reapplied for display-off/display-on wake versus full panel sleep and reset?
next_step: Compare these measurements with Claude’s cited source reports, then agree on discriminating experiments and their expected outcomes before changing functional driver behavior.
evidence_availability: The listed committed evidence files are included in the repository. Full dmesg, framebuffer and other device snapshots remain in the local private evidence directory.
